description: BOUN-SIM generates and monitors Session Initiation Protocol traffic for a Voice over IP network. Its contributors publish a Python simulator that makes synthetic subscribers call each other through a SIP server. A separate monitor can collect server and packet features, and the repository lists sample denial-of-service traffic. Users set the subscriber population, calling behaviour and server configuration; the resulting traffic covers that synthetic network and chosen run period, not a mapped service area. The software can support telecom security or capacity simulations when access to real SIP traces is limited. Public source is free under GPL-2.0. Its README names pjsip and provides an older virtual machine as an optional dependency route, which was not obtained. A limitation is that synthetic calling and attack patterns may differ from operating networks and need validation before training a monitor. No related catalogue record was identified. No SIP server, virtual machine or packet dataset was run.
name: BOUN-SIM SIP network simulator
notes: G5 G5-0947. The README lists a virtual-machine image and sample traffic data. Neither was downloaded. The article and code target Python 2.7 and older SIP-server settings; current compatibility was not checked.
